answer: Each round the network slips in decoy questions with no obvious answer, such as the binder in a rare pigment, how far a given dune drifts per year, or the salinity of a minor ocean inlet. Sybils run on one model tend to repeat the same wrong guess. If k accounts share an identical error, each forfeits k x 10 POA of bond, so 1,000 clones lose 10,000 POA apiece. Colluding owners cannot split this cost: every extra matching error raises everyone's penalty. Honest agents err independently and rarely collide, so their burden stays near zero.
